attachments.landmark_b: head, neck and tubercle of the rib

bands.name: Radiate ligament of the head of the rib

attachments.landmark_a: anterior aspect of the head of the rib
attachments.landmark_b: bodies of the two adjacent vertebrae and the intervening disc

bands.mechanical_role: binds the rib head to the vertebral column
bands.function_note: Its three fan-shaped bands are why the rib head is anchored to two vertebrae rather than one.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Intra-articular ligament of the head of the rib

attachments.landmark_b: intervertebral disc

bands.mechanical_role: divides the costovertebral joint into two synovial compartments
bands.function_note: Absent for ribs 1, 10, 11 and 12, whose heads articulate with a single vertebra.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Costotransverse ligament

attachments.landmark_b: transverse process of the corresponding vertebra

bands.mechanical_role: binds the rib neck to the transverse process
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Lateral costotransverse ligament

attachments.landmark_b: tip of the transverse process

bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Superior costotransverse ligament

attachments.landmark_a: crest of the neck of the rib
attachments.landmark_b: transverse process of the vertebra above

bands.function_note: Its lateral border helps bound the space through which the thoracic paravertebral block is placed.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

function: Bind each rib to the vertebral column at two points -- head and tubercle -- which together define the fixed axis about which the rib rotates in respiration. The orientation of that axis, more transverse above and more sagittal below, is what makes the upper ribs move in pump-handle and the lower in bucket-handle fashion.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

attachments.landmark_a: anterior and posterior surfaces, costal notches
attachments.landmark_b: costal cartilages 2-10

bands.name: Radiate sternocostal ligaments

attachments.landmark_b: anterior and posterior surfaces of the sternum, fanning out to blend with the periosteum

bands.mechanical_role: binds each costal cartilage to the sternum and, on the anterior surface, blends across the midline with the contralateral side to help form the membrana sterni
bands.function_note: The first costal cartilage is united to the sternum by a synchondrosis rather than a synovial joint and so has no radiate ligament of its own; ribs 2-7 each have one.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Costoxiphoid ligament

attachments.landmark_b: anterior and posterior surfaces of the xiphoid process

bands.mechanical_role: anchors the 7th costal cartilage to the xiphoid process at the inferior end of the sternocostal joint chain
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Interchondral ligaments

attachments.landmark_a: adjacent borders of costal cartilages 6-9 (occasionally to 10)
attachments.landmark_b: adjacent borders of the costal cartilage below

bands.mechanical_role: binds the false-rib costal cartilages to one another, forming the costal margin and contributing to the fixed articulated arch that supports the lower thoracic wall
bands.function_note: Small synovial or fibrous joints between the successive costal cartilages of ribs 6-9 (sometimes 10), distinct from the sternocostal joints proper; they are why the costal margin behaves as one continuous arch rather than separate cartilage tips.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

function: Bind the costal cartilages of ribs 2-7 to the lateral border of the sternum and, via the interchondral and costoxiphoid ligaments, unite the lower costal cartilages to each other and to the xiphoid process -- the anterior counterpart of the posterior costovertebral/costotransverse ligament complex.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
